rawFindings.title: Potential TypeError in slugize with non-string input
rawFindings.explanation: In the create() method, the code changed from explicitly converting data.slug or data.title to a string before passing to slugize() to directly passing data.slug or data.title without conversion. If data.slug or data.title is not a string (e.g., a number), slugize may throw an error or behave unexpectedly.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the toString() call on data.slug || data.title before passing to slugize to ensure input is always a string: data.slug = slugize((data.slug || data.title).toString(), {transform: config.filename_case});
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling post.create() with a numeric title (e.g., title: 12345) will cause slugize to throw a TypeError instead of generating a slug correctly.

rawFindings.title: Potential TypeError in slugize with non-string slug in publish()
rawFindings.explanation: In the publish() method, the code changed from converting data.slug to string before passing to slugize to passing it directly. If data.slug is not a string, slugize may throw an error or behave unexpectedly.
rawFindings.suggestion: Add toString() call on data.slug before slugize, restoring: var slug = data.slug = slugize(data.slug.toString(), {transform: config.filename_case});
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling post.publish() with a numeric slug (e.g., slug: 12345 as a number) will cause slugize to throw a TypeError instead of generating a slug correctly.
